content:
Hi all! Recently #39063 was merged. This is the key ingredient (well, its balanced version) to generalize the Banach open mapping theorem (docs#ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap) to F-spaces.

Is that worth adding? If so, the method would generally be:

  • Provide the missing background components (e.g., the image of an absorbent set is absorbent under certain conditions)
  • Move docs#ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap to a new file (e.g., FSpace.lean), but keep the name and just loosen the type classes
  • Migrate all the consequences to FSpace.lean as well (assuming they still apply)
  • In the end, leave the theorems like docs#ContinuousLinearMap.exists_approx_preimage_norm_le which are steps on the way to the open mapping theorem, but may be of independent interest.
What exactly is the statement of the theorem you want to prove ? In particular, what are the restrictions on the field ?

According to Bourbaki, this is really a theorem about metrizable TVSs over complete docs#NontriviallyNormedField. In particular, it should be possible to write down this proof without any reference to convexity.
(In fact I believe there is a statement about metrizable topological groups, but IIRC the proof is more complicated)

I have a proof of the following:

variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [UniformSpace E] [IsUniformAddGroup E]
    [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] [FirstCountableTopology E] [CompleteSpace E]
  [AddCommGroup F] [Module 𝕜 F] [UniformSpace F] [IsUniformAddGroup F]
    [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 F] [FirstCountableTopology F] [CompleteSpace F] [T2Space F]

theorem ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap'
    (f : E →L[𝕜] F) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : IsOpenMap f

It does require a generalization of #39063 to remove convexity and just keep the balanced bit (this an identical proof)
The proof is only 120 lines or so once you add in all the helpers (which are another 100 or so lines)
(You can generalize to the semilinear case pretty trivially...)

Thinking about it a bit more, I think I can get to the general topological group notion with substantially the same proof, but need to:

  • Replace the notion of Balanced with Symmetric (i.e., B = -B). This is currently not in mathlib (but shows up as a hypothesis in a few places);
  • Replace scalar multiplication by 𝕜 with a countable collection of "expansions" T : ι → E ≃ₜ E (resp. T' : ι → F ≃ₜ F) such that for any (closed) neighborhood U ∈ 𝓝 0 you have ⋃ i, T i '' s = univ and same for T'. I don't believe there's currently such a notion in mathlib; and
  • Replace f with a surjective homomorphism between the groups E and F which commutes with T/T', i.e. f (T n U) = T' n (f U).

Then all other cases follow by using scalar multiplication as the T and T' and making f (semi)-linear.

I believe these sorts of objects are studied in the literature, but I'm not familiar with them. So I'm happy to add this generalization, but couldn't vouch for it being the right API :-)

OK, I didn't go all the way to the topological group setting, but if it's of interest, I did clean up the actual proof as #41166 (specifically, here).

Not all of the lemmas in #40983 are actually needed, and #41166 goes a little farther and refactors out much of Banach.lean into the more general setting.

If it's of interest, happy to work to get it merged :-)
